messages.content: The first general-purpose electronic computer, ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), was built in 1946. It occupied 1,800 square feet, used 17,468 vacuum tubes, and could perform 5,000 additions per second—remarkably fast for its time. However, it required manual rewiring for different tasks, making it more of a "computing machine" than a modern computer.
